idea_summary: An application where customers book appointments with local service providers and providers manage availability.

functional_requirements.statement: Customers should be able to search and book appointments with local service providers.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can enter search criteria such as location, service type, date, and time.
A list of available local service providers is displayed based on the search criteria.
After selecting a service provider, a slot selection interface is shown with available booking slots.
Upon selecting a slot, a booking confirmation page is provided with all necessary details.

functional_requirements.statement: Local service providers should be able to manage their availability and book/approve appointments.
acceptance_criteria: Providers can view their calendar to manage their availability and add/approve/schedule appointments.
Providers can mark specific dates and times as unavailable or available for booking.
Providers receive notifications when new bookings are received.
Providers can approve or reject customer-provided notes and preferences.

functional_requirements.statement: Customers and providers should be able to cancel appointments within the applicable cancellation policy.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can view their booked appointments and initiate cancellation.
Providers can view booked appointments and take necessary actions (e.g., rescheduling, informing customers).
Both sides receive confirmation of the cancellation process.
A cancellation policy must be clearly communicated to customers and providers.

non_functional_requirements.statement: The application must prevent double bookings.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Automated unit tests and real-time system monitors for all booking operations.

non_functional_requirements.statement: The application must enforce role-based authorization between customers and providers.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Role-based access control (RBAC) testing with simulated user sessions.

non_functional_requirements.statement: The application must account for timezone differences when managing appointments.
non_functional_requirements.target: 100% accuracy in displaying and scheduling appointments across different time zones
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: User acceptance testing with diverse geographic representations.

non_functional_requirements.statement: The application must implement a robust cancellation policy with clear terms.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Comprehensive end-to-end user testing and audit trails.

non_functional_requirements.statement: The application must handle concurrent booking requests efficiently.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Load testing and stress testing with concurrent booking scenarios.

architecture_components.name: Frontend UI
responsibilities: User interface for customer and provider views

architecture_components.name: Backend API
responsibilities: API endpoints for customer and provider interactions
Business logic for booking, cancellation, and management

architecture_components.name: Database
responsibilities: Storage and retrieval of bookings and provider availability
Audit logs for security and compliance

architecture_components.name: Notification Service
responsibilities: Sending booking confirmations, cancellations, and updates to customers and providers

data_entities.name: Provider
data_entities.purpose: Stores information about local service providers

tests.description: Test for unauthorized access when role-based authorization fails

obligation_coverage.design_response: A unique booking identifier and a constraint on overlapping dates/times enforced on booking entities.
Role-based access control (RBAC) enforcing access based on user roles, leveraging JWT tokens.
Database stores time zone information and API operations perform time zone conversions as necessary.
Cancellation endpoints enforce specific business rules, and both sides receive confirmation of cancellation.
Load testing to verify 99.99% availability under simultaneous load, and handling of concurrent requests through appropriate concurrency control mechanisms.

assumptions.statement: Existing communication systems will support the push of booking notifications
